summary.intent: Test the new 'automate cards like this' routine feature end to end on a live inbox, and make the offer to write a routine visible right after a decision instead of hidden in a panel, then reset the port card so it can be re-tested.
summary.outcome: Added a post-decision bar offering 'Write a routine' that auto-opens the agent's draft with a prominent writing state, made routine names and descriptions buyer-friendly, backed up state, reset the port card and restarted the server, verified the flow headless via screenshots, and committed. Only src/ask_soony/routines.py is listed as modified.

repo: Live state is stored in state files (decisions and an action log). Resetting a card means removing its decision and its action entry, then restarting the server so new writer instructions load.

Approving a card option can send real external emails: the Hwaseong card option 0 emails Boise (~USD 196k air freight) and the Game Card 128 GB card option 0 emails Hwaseong. Only the port card option (internal message to the DC site lead) is safe for testing.
Routines run every 60 seconds in a sandbox that allows only `from soony import ...`, with no file or network access.
Routines that would trigger a costly option (e.g. Boise air freight) show 'Would tell you: ...' in the test run instead of sending (a money brake).
A routine acting on its own needs a second matching card; the first port card is consumed by the decision used to write the routine, so the test run shows 'Nothing in the inbox matches right now'.
Handled cards show 'via routine: ...' and appear in the routine's run log.

code.finding: Modified to make routine names and descriptions use buyer language (writer instructions changed); requires a server restart to take effect. Line numbers not given in the transcript.

workflow: Back up state files before resetting live data, then verify the reset afterwards.
Verify UI changes headlessly by running the flow and reading the screenshots (offer.png, draft.png).
Check live system state before giving test steps or resetting so the instructions match what is actually in the inbox.
Place offers where the decision happens rather than in hidden panels (user feedback on discoverability).

friction: The first test instructions had the user finding the automate option in a hidden Routines panel, which the user found unintuitive.
Testing against live data carries the risk of real emails going to suppliers, so the user must avoid approving two of the three cards.
Showing the routine acting autonomously needs a second matching card, and timing of new portal data is unpredictable.
open_items: Offered but not confirmed: adding a second port card from real data so the routine can be seen acting on its own.
The user still has to run the manual test (approve the port card, click 'Write a routine', turn it on) on the reset card.
Whether a second discharged container exists in the data to create another port card is unverified.
